title: Finite diagrams of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-complexes descend to a finite extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. All schemes and morphisms below are in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$, and morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Fix a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Qlb$; finite coefficient fields and their inclusions are [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Let $T$ be a scheme of this setting. For a finite $F\subset\Qlb$ or $F=\Qlb$, write $\Dbc(T,F)$ for the full bounded constructible condensed-module derived category [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and $K_F$, $K_{\Qlb}$ for derived coefficient extension [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. The extension-of-scalars cocone is a filtered $2$-colimit in the ordinary-category sense [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit], by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]. Then:

1. For $K,L\in\Dbc(T,E)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{F\supset E}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dbc(T,F)}(K_F,L_F[q])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dbc(T,\Qlb)}(K_{\Qlb},L_{\Qlb}[q])$$
is a bijection.
2. Every finite collection of objects and arrows in $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ satisfying finitely many specified equalities of composites is isomorphic to the extension of scalars of such a collection over one finite $F\supset E$, satisfying those same equalities. Here the isomorphism consists of object isomorphisms intertwining all the specified arrows; no assertion about infinitely many independent relations is made.
3. For every separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ in the setting, every finite $F\subset\Qlb$, $K\in\Dbc(X,F)$ and $M\in\Dbc(Y,F)$, there are natural isomorphisms
$$(Rf_{!,F}K)_{\Qlb}\simeq Rf_{!,\Qlb}(K_{\Qlb}),\qquad (f_F^*M)_{\Qlb}\simeq f_{\Qlb}^*(M_{\Qlb}).$$
Here $Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ for a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$ in the standing setting.

proof.text: Apply finiteCoefficientDescentTwoColimit at p = ringChar k. Its rational predicate equality turns each bounded constructible input K,L into a constant-model bounded constructible input without changing its underlying object. The theorem Hom clause gives exactly the required representative and eventual equality assertions, for every integer shift.

Use the filtered two-colimit cocone from the same theorem. Choose a model of every vertex, take an upper bound for their finitely many fields and the prescribed field E, and transport the vertex isomorphisms by the cocone transitivity isomorphisms. Induct over the finite set of generating arrows. Hom surjectivity lifts the next conjugated arrow over a later field; extend every previous arrow along that transition and transport its commutative square by naturality of the cocone isomorphism. The path-category universal construction assembles these arrows into a functor, and induction on paths proves naturality of the vertex isomorphisms. For every specified relation, naturality and its equality in the vertex category imply equality after scalar extension. Faithfulness of derived scalar extension to the closure then implies the relation already over the resulting field. Empty vertices or arrows are covered by the empty finite family and the empty induction. This follows the finite object/arrow/relation descent in the blueprint, using the stronger existing faithfulness interface to avoid further enlargement for relations.

For pullback, restrict the published derivedPullIso for the actual finite-subfield inclusion to the full bounded constructible categories; its ambient naturality is the required naturality. For compact support use the very chosen compactification defining boundedConstructibleLowerShriek. Open extension preserves bounded constructibility, hence its input to proper pushforward is bounded below. Apply isIso_derivedPushHom_padicAlgCl_of_boundedBelow to this input and the proper part. Compose the direct-image component isomorphism with the proper pushforward of derivedOpenImmersionShriekIso. Naturality follows by composing the naturality squares of these two transformations. The compatibility isomorphisms of the restricted functors identify both composites with their ambient versions, and full faithfulness of the inclusion restricts this natural isomorphism back to bounded constructible categories. This is precisely the proper/open comparison of blueprint (3), specialized directly to the closure inclusion without the general scalar-six coherence package.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $E/\Ql$ finite. By [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] the
condensed category $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ is the $2$-colimit of the categories
$\Dbc(T,F)$ over finite extensions $F\supset E$ inside $\Qlb$, along the
extension-of-scalars functors; this is a theorem, not a definition. Then:

1. for $K,L\in\Dbc(T,E)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$,
   $\varinjlim_{F\supset E}\Hom_{\Dbc(T,F)}(K_F,L_F[q])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{\Dbc(T,\Qlb)}(K_{\Qlb},L_{\Qlb}[q])$;
2. every finite diagram in $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ (finitely many objects and
   morphisms) satisfying finitely many relations (equalities of composites) is
   isomorphic to the extension of scalars of a diagram over some finite
   $F\supset E$ satisfying the same relations;
3. for $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, the functors $Rf_{!,\Qlb}$ and
   $f^*_{\Qlb}$ commute with extension of scalars from each finite $F$.

proof.text:
(1) In a filtered $2$-colimit of categories, Hom sets between images of objects
from one stage are the filtered colimits of the Hom sets at later stages; apply
this to $K$ and $L[q]$.

(2) Each object of the $2$-colimit comes from some stage, and by (1) each
morphism between objects coming from a stage $F$ comes from a later stage. With
finitely many objects and morphisms, a common finite $F$ suffices (the system
of finite extensions inside $\Qlb$ is filtered). Each relation is an equality
of two morphisms after extension to $\Qlb$, hence by (1) holds already after
extension to some finite $F'$; finitely many relations hold over a common
$F''$.

(3) Extension of scalars from $F$ to $\Qlb$ commutes with pullback (pullback
of module sheaves commutes with tensor products with the constant coefficient
sheaf) and with $j_!$ (exact), and with $R\bar f_*$ for proper $\bar f$ on bounded
constructible objects (the coefficient comparison for $E\to\Qlb$ of
[sk-prop-scalar-six]). Hence $Rf_{!,\Qlb}$
and $f^*_{\Qlb}$ commute with extension of scalars.
